result.summary:
Independently re-checked docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-036.md against handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-03-test-designer.json, gh issue #68's full text/8 ACs, docs/agents/design/REQ-036.md, and the actual shipped implementation (apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/urgencyJobs.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts). All 8 ACs have at least one precise, mechanically-followable case; no TODOs found.

AC-by-AC verification performed:

- AC1: File 1 describe('AC1') constructs an event exactly 48h out and a second 49h out in the SAME test, asserting both the push (sent.length, tgId, event-A title) and the list marker (listPendingRequestsForOrganizer's isUrgent) for both timings. Confirmed listPendingRequestsForOrganizer/isRequestUrgent are real, already-shipped functions (registration.ts:1597-1636, event.ts:785-787) with signatures matching the spec's call sites exactly.

- AC2: Traced the fixture by hand -- seedPendingRequest x3 (pending1-3) + seedPendingRequest x2 then approveRequest/rejectRequest (toAdmit, toReject) genuinely create 5 distinct registration rows (registerForEvent confirmed to always return 'requested' for requiresApproval:true regardless of seatsLeft, matching the comment's cited precedent). approveRequest/rejectRequest signatures (registration.ts:1753, 1877) match the spec's call arguments exactly. The admitted/rejected rows are asserted UNCHANGED via a direct admission-value re-read (toBe('admitted')/toBe('rejected')) AND a zero-new-audit-row check for both -- not merely 'still present'. Audit count is captured before and after (auditBefore/auditAfter) and asserted to differ by exactly 3.

- AC4 (restart-safety, deepest check): confirmed by tracing both scheduler/autoDeclineJobs.ts's makeAutoDeclineJob loop and domain/registration.ts's autoDeclineRequest (lines 1960-2006) line by line, and cross-referencing SECURITY-REVIEWER's own step-02c restart trace (handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-02c-security-reviewer.json), which performed an identical kill-mid-batch trace independently and reached the same conclusion. Neither the job loop nor autoDeclineRequest nor selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline retains ANY in-memory state across separate .run() invocations -- every tick re-queries registrations.admission and events.* fresh from Postgres with no cache, no closure-captured mutable state, no timer/interval bookkeeping consulted by the selection query itself. A genuine process kill-and-restart differs from an in-process second .run() call ONLY in whether the OS process and its heap are torn down -- and since this job's correctness depends entirely on committed Postgres state (Mechanism 2: admission='requested' re-selection filter) and a second independent committed Postgres structure (Mechanism 1: notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind)), neither of which lives in process memory, there is no code path a real restart would exercise that a same-process double .run() call does not. This is the same conclusion noShowJobs.db.test.ts's REQ-032 AC3 precedent already established for a structurally identical job shape, and the same conclusion SECURITY-REVIEWER reached by reading the code independently. The test's assertions (sent.length still 3 after run 2, all rows still 'rejected', zero further audit rows, ledger still exactly one row per registration) are precisely AC4's literal count requirement. VERDICT: sound, no gap found.

- AC5: describe('AC5') contains two `it`s as claimed -- one evaluationTime shortly AFTER endsAt (auto-declines, asserts registrationClosesAt still null / no column added), one evaluationTime BEFORE endsAt (asserts sent.length 0 and admission still 'requested'). Both branches of the fallback genuinely exercised. Cross-checked against the shipped selectRegistrationsForAutoDecline's OR-branch (autoDeclineJobs.ts:59-62): matches exactly.

- AC7: confirmed via domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification (lines 111-168) that the blocked check (step 2, line 122) executes strictly before the ledger INSERT (step 4, line 136) -- so a blocked registrant genuinely gets a real admission transition + audit row (autoDeclineRequest runs and commits regardless of notification outcome, since the job only skips the SEND when outcome.kind==='reject' is already true) but zero ledger row, exactly as the File 2 AC7 case asserts (rowB admission 'rejected', auditB length 1, ledgerB length 0). The transition-happens/send-skipped distinction is asserted precisely, not conflated.

- AC8: apps/bot/src/i18n/catalogs.test.ts read directly -- confirmed it is a generic flatten-and-compare check (flattens the full ru/en objects and asserts identical sorted key sets, plus non-empty-string checks) with no requirement-specific logic, so it structurally already covers the new organizerRequests.urgentMarker/urgentNotification and autoDecline.notification keys with no changes needed. The grep-based case in File 2 was verified against the actual shipped source: urgencyJobs.ts contains 'getCatalog(lang)' (line 89) and does not contain the literal 'still pending 48 hours'; autoDeclineJobs.ts contains 'catalog.autoDecline.notification' (line 92) and does not contain the literal 'was not decided before registration closed' -- both assertions verified true against real file content, not assumed. The provisional-wording disclosure was independently confirmed present in handoffs/WF02-REQ-036/step-02-backend-dev.json's result.issues[0] (exact quoted text found).

- AC3 honest-wording check: read apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts's actual autoDecline.notification string ('...was not decided before registration closed, so it could not be approved. Nobody reviewed and declined it -- the window simply closed before a decision was made.') and confirmed the spec's two toContain() assertions are literal substrings of it. Confirmed the spec ALSO asserts absence of blame language via four explicit negative substring checks ('you were not accepted', 'not good enough', 'not qualified', 'your application') -- genuine mechanical absence checks, not merely presence-of-good-wording. Confirmed deepLinkSeeUpcoming's exact string ('See what's coming up with /events') matches en.ts line 74 verbatim.

- tg_id ranges: grepped every 'let nextTgId'/'let tgSeq' declaration across apps/bot/src myself (25 files). Highest prior band confirmed at 1_021_000_000 (organizerRequests.db.test.ts). The spec's claimed 1_030_000_000+ and 1_031_000_000+ bands do not collide with any of the 25 existing bands found.

All function signatures the spec's test code calls (createEvent, publishEvent, resolveOrCreateUser, registerForEvent, approveRequest, rejectRequest, listPendingRequestsForOrganizer, makeUrgencyNoticeJob, makeAutoDeclineJob) were checked directly against their real, shipped implementations -- all match exactly, confirming these cases exercise real functions, not aspirational/planned ones.
